related_questions.question: What are the side effects of the COVID booster?

text_blocks.snippet: Common side effects of a COVID-19 booster shot are similar to those experienced after the initial vaccination series and are generally mild and short-lived. These can include pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, and nausea. Swollen lymph nodes may also occur, and can last for up to 10 days, according to Yale New Haven Health. These reactions are typically most noticeable in the first 1-2 days after vaccination and then subside.
snippet_highlighted_words: pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, and nausea

text_blocks.snippet: To help manage any side effects, you can:

list.snippet: Apply a cool, damp cloth to the injection site: This can help reduce pain and swelling.
Drink plenty of fluids: Staying hydrated can help with fatigue and other symptoms.

Take an over-the-counter pain reliever: If you have no contraindications, acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help with pain and fever. According to the CDC, it's not recommended to take pain relievers before vaccination.
